title: How long does a turnover clean take? Benchmarks from 31,000 cleans, plus a same-day turnover playbook
summary: Turnover clean times by bedrooms from 31,000 timed cleans, how often same-day turnovers happen, and a copyable same-day turnover playbook.
body_markdown:
[All posts](https://prohost.ai/blog)


**A turnover clean takes about two hours. Across 30,985 timed turnover cleans, the median was 120 minutes from start to finish, and 1 in 10 took nearly 5 hours. Size drives most of the spread: a studio or one-bedroom takes about 85 minutes, a five-bedroom about 200. And half of all checkouts are same-day turnovers, where the cleaner has a median window of 5 hours and finishes after the next guest's check-in time about 1 time in 6.**


## Key takeaways


- **Median turnover clean: 120 minutes.** The middle half of cleans take **74 to 200 minutes** ; the slowest 10% take **4.9 hours or more** .
- **By size:** studio or 1 bedroom **85 min** , 2 bedrooms **106** , 3 bedrooms **146** , 4 bedrooms **165** , 5+ bedrooms **201** (medians).
- **49% of checkouts are same-day turnovers** : the next guest checks in the same day. For studios and one-bedrooms it's **56%** ; for 5+ bedrooms, **34%** .
- **On a same-day turnover the window is short.** The median gap between checkout time and the next check-in time is **5 hours** , and cleaners start a median **63 minutes** after checkout.
- **82% of same-day cleans finish before the next check-in time.** The slowest 10% finish **36 minutes or more** after it.

## Where we're coming from


I spent 6 years at Airbnb as a staff data scientist on the hosting team, and we host in Hawaii, the Smokies and Joshua Tree. Turnovers are the part of hosting guests never see and always notice. "How long should a clean take?" is one of the most common questions new hosts ask us, and most answers online are guesses. So we measured it.


> **How we measured it.** Turnover cleans completed in ProhostAI between November 19, 2025 and November 19, 2026, at 146 rental businesses and 2,249 listings. We kept only cleans where the cleaner tapped **Start** and **Complete** in the app and the time between was 10 minutes to 12 hours: 30,985 cleans. (About 22,500 more were marked done less than a minute after being started, so they carry no real duration.) The bedroom figures cover the 30,334 of those cleans whose listing is still on file. The time is start-to-finish, so it includes breaks and photo uploads. Same-day turnovers come from 398,510 confirmed checkouts at 12,556 single-unit listings at 843 businesses, using each listing's local date. Internal and test workspaces are excluded, and no single business is more than 8% of the cleans. Across the 75 businesses with at least 30 timed cleans, the median business's median clean was 132 minutes, close to the overall number.


## How long a turnover clean takes


Median turnover clean time in minutes, by number of bedrooms


Bedrooms Fastest quarter Median Slowest quarter starts at Slowest 10% starts at Listings


Studio or 1 57 min 85 min 132 min 206 min 710


2 71 min 106 min 163 min 248 min 571


3 89 min 146 min 230 min 310 min 510


4 105 min 165 min 253 min 335 min 246


5+ 127 min 201 min 279 min 363 min 212


Use the median as your planning number and the slowest-quarter number as your buffer. If your three-bedroom cleans routinely run past 230 minutes, something specific is slowing them down: laundry done on site, a hot tub to drain, a long drive between properties, or a checklist that grew without anyone pruning it.


## Half of all checkouts are same-day turnovers


Share of checkouts followed by a check-in the same day, by number of bedrooms


**49%** of checkouts were followed by a check-in at the same listing on the same day. Another **16%** had a check-in the next day. Smaller units turn over same-day more often, likely because they book shorter, more back-to-back stays. At the typical business, about **41%** of checkouts are same-day.


On those days the clock is tight:


Same-day turnovers (15,822 timed cleans) Median


Window from checkout time to next check-in time 5.0 hours


Cleaner starts after checkout time 63 minutes


Clean duration 111 minutes


Time to spare before check-in 94 minutes


Finished before the next check-in time 82% of cleans


Cleaners work faster on same-day turnovers (111 minutes, against 128 on other turnovers), and the typical one finishes with an hour and a half to spare. The problem is the tail. About 1 in 6 same-day cleans finished after the next guest's check-in time, and the slowest 10% finished 36 minutes or more late. That's the guest waiting in the driveway, or walking in on a cleaner.


## The same-day turnover playbook (copy this)


**The week before**


1. List every same-day turnover for the next 7 days, with the checkout time, the check-in time and the window in hours.
2. Flag any window under 4 hours, any 3+ bedroom same-day turnover, and any day with two same-day turnovers for the same cleaner.
3. Confirm the cleaner for each flagged day by name. Line up a backup.
4. Turn off early check-in and late checkout on same-day dates.


**The day before**


1. Send the departing guest checkout instructions with the checkout time in bold, plus a short list (dishes in the dishwasher, towels in the tub, trash out). A guest who leaves on time gives your cleaner back the first hour.
2. Make sure linens and supplies for the property are clean and on site.


**Turnover day**


1. Cleaner taps **Start** on arrival. If they haven't started 90 minutes after checkout, someone calls them.
2. Work in the same order every time: strip beds and start laundry first, then kitchen, bathrooms, bedrooms, living areas, floors last. A[room-by-room checklist](https://prohost.ai/blog/airbnb-cleaning-checklist) keeps the order.
3. Photos of each room on finish, then **Complete** .
4. Tell the arriving guest the place is ready, and if it's early, that they're welcome to come in.


**If it's running late**


1. Message the arriving guest before their check-in time, not after: say when it will be ready, and offer luggage drop-off or a nearby suggestion.
2. Afterwards, look at why. Was the start late, the clean long, or the window too short to begin with?

## FAQ


### How long should an Airbnb turnover clean take?


In our data the median was 120 minutes, and it scales with size: about 85 minutes for a studio or one-bedroom, 106 for two bedrooms, 146 for three, 165 for four and about 200 for five or more.


### What is a same-day turnover?


A day when one guest checks out and the next checks in at the same property. In our data, 49% of checkouts were same-day turnovers.


### How much time is there between checkout and check-in?


On same-day turnovers, the median window between the departing guest's checkout time and the next guest's check-in time was 5 hours.


### How often do cleans run late?


About 1 in 6 same-day cleans finished after the next guest's check-in time. The median clean finished with 94 minutes to spare.


### How do I make turnovers faster?


Start sooner after checkout, run the same room order every time, keep linens and supplies on site, and prune the checklist. On same-day turnovers, cleaners started a median of an hour after checkout, and that hour is often the easiest one to win back.


## The takeaway


Plan two hours for a typical clean, more for big homes, and treat every same-day turnover as a deadline. Most cleans finish with time to spare. The work is in catching the 1 in 6 that don't before the guest is at the door.
